messages:
deploy-bot: :rocket: Canary deploy started: release=v3.2.1, cohort=canary-5pct, started_by=ci-pipeline

emma (oncall): Seeing an alert — error rate spike on inference API P95 tokens. Paging oncall.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — svc/inference 5xx-rate > 3% for 2m (alert-id: A-1193). Escalating to oncall (emma).

emma (oncall): I'm on it. Pulling traces and canary logs. Can someone confirm which model variant was rolled? @raj?

raj: v2-quantized-8bit was included in the canary group. I can pull the rollout config.

maya: Noticed increased tail latency on canary hosts in us-west-2, and a bunch of OOM+retry logs in sidecar.

emma (oncall): OK — hypothesis: new quantized kernel causing instability under certain sequence lengths. Need to stop rollout and roll back canary. First try automated rollback.

deploy-bot: Attempting automated canary rollback (policy: immediate on critical errors). Exec status: FAILED — feature-flag block present (flag: enable_rollback_v3_2_1=false).

emma (oncall): Ugh — rollback blocked by feature flag that was left disabled in config. @raj did we gate rollback in the pipeline?

raj: The flag is customer-facing kill-switch; ops flagged it to avoid accidental rollbacks earlier. I misread the runbook, my bad.

emma (oncall): We need a manual rollback then. @maya can you stage the manual undo? I'll coordinate communications and impact assessment.

maya: Starting manual rollback. Steps: 1) scale up previous replica set 2) drain new pods 3) mark canary traffic zero. Running commands now.

maya: Running: ```kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference --to-revision=42 --namespace=prod```

ops-bot: Runbook-check: manual rollback requires approval from oncall + prod-safety. Emma please acknowledge to proceed.

emma (oncall): Ack, proceed. Marking incident channel for customers. Posting notice to status page: "We are rolling back a recent canary deployment due to elevated errors. Some requests may see transient failures."

deploy-bot: Rollout undo triggered. new pods terminating, previous pods scaling up (rc:42).

maya: Old pods are healthy, readiness probes passing. Draining canary pods.

raj: Pushing quick feature-flag flip as extra safety: setting enable_new_quant_kernel=false across canary groups to prevent immediate re-exposure. Command: ```redwood-ffctl set enable_new_quant_kernel false --scope=canary-5pct```

emma (oncall): Good. Now verification: running synthetic smoke tests against control and previously affected endpoints.

sre-runbook-bot: Verification checklist: 1) 5xx rate < 0.5% over 5m 2) P95 latency back to baseline 3) No OOM logs 4) Customers with errors < 50 in last 5m.

maya: Smoke tests: endpoint /v1/generate returned 200 for 100/100 requests. P95 latency trending down from 1.9s -> 0.6s on canary hosts now.

raj: Error counts dropping. Error-rate metric shows 0.4% over last 5m window. OOM logs no longer appearing in new pod logs.

ops-bot: Customer impact summary: ~120 failed requests tied to canary group in the 10 minutes after deploy. No single tenant exceeds SLA breach threshold; no high-severity customer pages yet.

emma (oncall): Good catch. I'll escalate to customer success for proactive outreach to any customers who reported anomalies. Putting incident into recovery state and creating a short postmortem task.

jordan (oncall-next): Taking handoff — what's outstanding?

emma (oncall): Handoff notes: rollback completed manually due to FF block, verification checklist passed, flagged config issue (rollback FF) as root cause contributor, create follow-ups: (1) remove rollback block or adjust policy, (2) add automated guardrail to flip FF on critical failures, (3) add additional model kernel canary tests.

jordan (oncall-next): Got it. I'll own the follow-ups for 24h. Also locking the release: tag v3.2.1 as quarantined.

raj: I'll open an internal PR to update the pipeline and fix the flag workflow.

emma (oncall): Thanks team. Filing incident ticket INC-2026-314 and linking this thread. We'll do a full postmortem in the morning. :coffee:

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident moved to "resolved (under monitoring)" by emma (oncall).
